Subject: Hosted API pricing for high sustained throughput

Hi Michael,

We reviewed Redwood's public hosted API pricing and want to understand how you would price for the following profile: roughly 8B tokens/month sustained for 6+ months, with occasional spikes up to ~12–13B tokens. Key questions from Procurement & Engineering: 

- Do you offer any smoothing (month-to-month averaging) vs strict monthly band billing?
- What discounting is available for sustained throughput vs short-term bursts?
- Can burst capacity be bought as a separate pool rather than pushing the committed band?
- How do true-ups and annualized commitments work?

I've attached our latest usage projection CSV. Procurement's timeline is 3–4 weeks for terms + signature. Would love a high-level rate card and one-sentence explanation of how smoothing / burst pools would be handled.

Thanks,
Sanjay Patel
Head of Cloud Integrations
RetailOne

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear note and the projection. I looped in Laura (Sales Ops) and Ben (Pricing) to put together a concise proposal. High level answers up front:

- Yes, we support month-to-month smoothing (we call it an "overage smoothing" window) that averages consumption across a rolling 3-month window for billing purposes; this prevents single-month spikes from moving you into a higher permanent band.
- We can offer a dedicated burst pool (pre-paid) to handle short spikes; usage from the burst pool is billed at the same discounted rate as the committed band until the pool is exhausted.
- Deepest discounts come with an annualized commit; we can offer a blended rate if you want lower upfront commit but still want smoothing.

I'll attach an initial draft of a staggered-bands rate sheet for your team to review. Laura will follow up with numeric bands and sample invoice math. If you prefer, we can get time on the calendar this week to walk through scenarios.

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Hi Sanjay — following up with a concrete proposal to address the points you raised. Below is a concise rate card and operational notes (summary; attached PDF has line-item math).

Proposed structure (staggered consumption bands + smoothing):
- Band A (0–2B tokens / month): $0.0035 per 1k tokens
- Band B (2–6B tokens / month): $0.0026 per 1k tokens
- Band C (6–10B tokens / month): $0.0020 per 1k tokens
- Band D (10B+ tokens / month): $0.0016 per 1k tokens (applies only when an annualized commit >= $1.5M is signed)

Operational controls:
- Over-smoothing: rolling 3-month average for billing to avoid single-month band escalations.
- Burst pool: pre-paid pool that sits on top of the committed band; charged at the Band C rate until consumed. Pool sizes are configurable (we suggested 2B tokens/month burst pool).
- True-up: At quarter close we true-up actual usage vs committed baseline; credits apply to next invoice if you paid for more than used.
- Overage smoothing cap: we can cap effective monthly overage recognized via smoothing at +25% of baseline to limit unbounded charge jumps.
- SLA credits: latency/availability credits tied to sustained throughput SLOs are available for Dedicated customers; for Hosted we can include limited uptime credits for account-level thresholds.

Sample economics: attached PDF contains examples for your 8B sustained profile with and without a 12B burst pool. TL;DR: with a 12-month annualized commit we can migrate you to Blended Band C/D pricing and reduce effective per-1k cost by ~18–27% vs on-demand.

Next steps we recommend:
1) Confirm desired burst pool size and whether you want an annualized commit window (12 or 24 months).
2) If Procurement wants standard terms, we'll send a redlineable MSA with a committed consumption schedule.
3) We can provide a sample invoice/line-item calc for your month-zero forecast (Ben is on this thread and will drop that in).

Thanks — happy to jump on a call Wednesday if that works.

—Laura
